note: Remaining concerns of #1488 and #1757, observed ALONGSIDE the existing journeys from the evidence the approved harness already records (guard logs, step logs, case results, receipts). No new campaign, no new stimulus, no new product traffic, $0. A concern is reported as OBSERVED CLEAN, OBSERVED PROBLEM or NOT OBSERVABLE per sub-observation; the concern's verdict is PROBLEM if any sub-observation is a problem, else NOT OBSERVABLE if any could not be observed, else CLEAN. Missing visibility is not proof of safety and is not a product failure. The text of the PRs is not part of this package: the concerns below are those named in the Product Owner's addendum.

concerns.title: Results are bound to the actual deployed SHA
concerns.brief: Every identity read before and after each journey, and at the end, must MATCH the tested SHA, and the results' own source and served SHA must be it.
reproduction: Run any journey under the approved harness (execute_run.sh stages build-plan to collect) so identity reads are taken before and after it.
Run scripts/check_coverage.py on the sealed case-results.json: deployedVersionBinding lists every receipt checked and every mismatch.
Compare the served SHA in each identityBefore/identityAfter receipt with release.testedSha of the request.

concerns.title: Worker cleanup and outbound requests after termination
concerns.brief: After a journey's step completes and its browser is terminated: no owned process remains, no request starts after termination, and worker cleanup is observable.
reproduction: Run the journey under the approved harness; its step.log records 'step completed' and 'stop ... remaining N'.

In guard.jsonl, list request events whose time minus ms (their start) is later than 'step completed': those started after termination. Requests that started earlier and finished within milliseconds were in flight at termination.
Service-worker and web-worker lifetimes are not visible to the guard (only worker and audioworklet script loads are): see the NOT OBSERVABLE sub-observation.

concerns.title: Native-form, EventSource and telemetry traffic carries no unexpected payload
concerns.brief: Native form submissions, EventSource streams and telemetry requests must not carry unexpected payloads.
reproduction: Run the journey under the approved harness; guard.jsonl records every request (method, destination type, navigation flag, rule, status, bytes) and every refused connection by host.
Native form submission = a navigation (nav true, destination document) with a method other than GET or HEAD.

Request bodies, request headers and response content types are not recorded, so payload content and EventSource streams cannot be inspected from the guard log; telemetry hosts are refused by the guard policy before any TLS exchange.

concerns.title: Logs and reports retain no raw test sentinels, transcripts or sensitive payloads
concerns.brief: The sealed receipts, logs and generated reports must not contain the raw stimulus sentinels (focus topic and points), transcript text fields, tokens, provider keys or e-mail addresses.
reproduction: Run scripts/derive_concerns.py on the sealed run: it scans every retained file of the run (and the control-plane outputs) for the sentinel texts of the fixture manifest, secret patterns and transcript-like text fields.
A finding is reported as file, sha256, pattern id and count; the matched text itself is never written to any output.
Re-run the scan on the generated report directory with scripts/derive_concerns.py --scan-dir <report dir> to check the outputs too.

concerns.title: Protections do not disrupt legitimate telemetry or normal user journeys
concerns.brief: Whether the protections of #1488 and #1757 disturb legitimate telemetry or the normal journeys.
reproduction: Run the full journeys under the approved harness and compare each journey's verdicts with the last known good run (scripts/select_baselines.py, scripts/derive_alerts.py).
Count telemetry connection attempts per journey in guard.jsonl (kind connect, telemetry hosts) in this run and the previous run.
The harness refuses telemetry hosts by policy, so whether telemetry would be accepted by its provider cannot be observed from this harness.
